  Yes:  7 Amick, Boyce, Diles III, Martins, Shuford, Wee, Rockenbach

  • Dalton Dorr from the Health Department provided an update on the 2025
  Point-In-Time Count report, which was conducted on January 23, 2025. The
  count identified a total of 3,595 people experiencing homelessness in the
  city, reflecting a net increase of 219 individuals compared to 2024.
  Additionally, 167 people were reported displaced due to the Southern
  California wildfires.
  Key findings include:
  • 390 individuals were identified as newly homeless in the area.
  • The proportion of vehicular homelessness rose to 38.7%.
  • The percentage of Latinx individuals experiencing homelessness decreased
  from 28.4% to 24.1% compared to last year.
  • The number of veterans experiencing homelessness also decreased in
  2025.
  • The number of people sheltered in 2025 increased compared to 2024.
  • The riverbed population is characterized as a slightly different group,
  generally younger, predominantly male, and Latinx.
  • Staff commented on potential upcoming cuts and the possible displacement
  effects due to reductions in Emergency Housing Vouchers (EHV), noting this
  could significantly impact the community. A plan is being developed to
  address these budgetary challenges.
  • Board members engaged in discussion with staff regarding housing
  affordability and concerns surrounding the uncertainty faced by
  undocumented individuals.

3.  25-55349  Recommendation to hold a discussion regarding stakeholder representation and

  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 5  Brezenoff, Lock, McFadzen, Tan, Topolewski

  • Jeffrey Proctor, Homeless Services Administrative Officer, provided an
  update on the recent amendments and revisions to the HSAC charter and
  bylaws, noting that the recommended changes—particularly those related to
  board seat composition—are consistent with existing written policies and
  procedures.
  • The currently vacant ESG-designated seat will now be expanded to include
  CoC Subrecipients as eligible representatives.
  • Pat Scott, the HSAC representative, was confirmed to fill the board seat
  previously held by Kimberly Lewis.
  • Board member Nikki raised concerns regarding the ESG-designated seat
  requirement. In response, staff will forward the updated charter to the City
  Attorney's Office for final review and approval.
  • The item was approved by roll call vote, pending final approval from the City
  Attorney.
